relations.argument: After fixing D, put U=D^2+sum_i Pstar(z_i,w_i)^2 with private rational witness blocks. In the ordered fieldQ each summand is nonnegative, so a zero forces D=0 and every Pstar=0. The separately supplied Pstar theorem forces all z_i integer. Conversely integer D witnesses have independent Pstar rational witnesses. This gives the fixed universal polynomial for all ordinary e,n>=0. Any c.e. set is the halting domain of a machine in the fixed syntactic enumeration; fixing that index gives its representation. The Pstar theorem is not proved by DPRM.
relations.limits: No explicit universal-polynomial coefficients are required, and no Pstar degree/height/arity estimate transfers to U.

relations.argument: The fixed finite integer coefficient list of U can be hard-coded. Given e, substitute e into its two ordinary parameters, compute its finite coefficient list and output the polynomial code; this is a total computable reduction of diagonal halting to HTP(Q). No uniform algorithm extracting a DPRM polynomial from a predicate is needed. Conversely compile from a valid polynomial code a machine that ignores its input, enumerates all rational tuples in its finite arity and evaluates exactly, halting on a zero. Its syntactic index is computable and diagonal input is ignored. Invalid codes map to one fixed nonhalting index; constant and zero-arity polynomials can be evaluated directly or treated with a dummy rational variable. Rational-coefficient coding is reduced by effective nonzero denominator clearing.
relations.limits: The mere undecidability corollary on sourcep3 is insufficient for this fixed universal construction. The representation theorem supplies it; the many-one reductions are the explicit local algorithms. This remains conditional on the Pstar integer definition.

rows.source_role: retained conditional cyclic-support inputs plus local projector and finite-character construction
rows.argument: The actual cyclic subgroup is a rank-one Z/p^e module. The accepted lattice-pair model makes its stabilizing order the specified Eichler order. On the stipulated split unit support, odd-p spectral projectors are integral; at2 use integral (1+x)/2 and eigenvalue difference r, a unit. A cyclic module admits only the two idempotents0,1, so exactly one projector selects the root. Unit scaling fixes the projectors and scales that root. For odd p, the cyclic2-primary subgroup of F_p^* has a character nontrivial on its order-two element; inflate it. At2 the character modulo4 gives negative parity. These finite character choices are elementary local constructions, not newform existence inputs.
rows.limits: The source is the cyclic subgroup itself, not the complementary quotient. Support and actual admissibility are explicit; the global Atkin operation remains separate.

rows.argument: Apply the unramified quadratic cyclic division model at the actual ell0. Its maximal-order residue is F_(ell0²); conjugation by order units is trivial on that commutative residue field, while a division uniformizer acts by its nontrivial Frobenius. For a nonzero trace-zero beta, Frobenius(beta)=-beta. If beta² were a square over F_ell0, beta would lie in F_ell0, impossible since ell0 is odd. As ell0=3 mod4, both -1 and beta² are nonsquares. Thus -t² beta² is square and Legendre(t) changes by -1 under Frobenius. Compact-open support and local constancy follow from the finite residue conditions.
rows.limits: Uses the actual division place ell0 and ell0=3 mod4, plus (m/ell0)=1 for the final D condition; does not identify an unrelated geometric normalizer.
